text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Thirty-six people in the Eastern district of Marsabit are killed by armed raiders from Ethiopia.
- Former Nairobi mayor John King'ori says the city council had not approved the sale of the disputed plot of land in Kigali street, Nairobi, to the Jamia Mosque.
- Two suspected witches in the Western Kenya district of Nyamira are beheaded by angry villagers.
- Students from Kinare High School, central Kenya, where students confessed to lesbianism, recount harrowing encounters with alleged marauding ghosts.

- A team of British Airways investigators fly in from London to check the security at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport after a stowaway youth perished on board the airline's Sunday flight to Gatwick.
- Presidential hopeful Charity Ngilu says she will form her own party if the Democratic Party (DP), to which she belongs, bars her from running in this year's general election.
- Seven DP branches warn the party leadership against declaring the national chairman Mwai Kibaki, the automatic presidential candidate.
- The German government donates 6,000 tonnes of maize worth 100 million shillings ($1.8 million) for distribution in famine- stricken areas in Kenya.
